Aristocrat

uh-RIS-tuh-krat · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Aristocrat is a member of the highest social class, especially one who holds hereditary rank, title, or privilege.

Raised in a castle with servants for every task, the young aristocrat had never once cooked her own meal.

Worked Example

Though the family had lost most of its fortune, they still carried themselves like aristocrats, insisting on formal manners at every meal.

Being an aristocrat is usually about birth and inherited title, not necessarily about how much money someone currently has.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

noble: a person of high hereditary rank or title

blueblood: a member of a family of high social standing

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

commoner: a person without noble rank or title

proletariat: the working class

Where it sits · how high the social rank sits — upper class → aristocrat → royalty

upper class vs. aristocrat: Upper class is a broad, general term for wealthy or high-status people, without necessarily implying an inherited title.

royalty vs. aristocrat: Royalty goes further still, referring specifically to kings, queens, and their immediate families -- the very top of the aristocracy.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — aristo-

root — aristo-: best (Greek aristos, 'best')

suffix — -crat

suffix — -crat: one who rules or has power (Greek kratos, 'power, rule')

Put it together

Put it together: Aristocrat comes from Greek aristos ('best') + -crat ('ruler') -- literally 'rule by the best,' referring to a hereditary class once believed to be naturally superior.

Use the root in a new word: aristocracy

Use the root in a new word: aristocracy: The aristocracy is the social class made up of aristocrats -- in Britain, it historically included dukes, earls, and other titled nobility.
